findings.title: Structural drift: ownership
findings.body:
Standard: .trellis/spec/apps/dashboard/frontend/api-layer-contract.md §1（禁止「在本模块里放**模块级单例**」）/ §2（`createTokenMutation(client: QueryClient)`，不要闭包模块单例）
Note: The archived design declares a module-level `queryClient` export in `lib/query-client.ts`, which the shipped contract forbids: the application instance must be created by a factory/injection (`createQueryClient({ onAuthExpired })`) and passed explicitly, otherwise tests and production share one cache and invalidation assertions become meaningless.
findings.recommendation: Align placement / naming / ownership with .trellis/spec/apps/dashboard/frontend/api-layer-contract.md §1（禁止「在本模块里放**模块级单例**」）/ §2（`createTokenMutation(client: QueryClient)`，不要闭包模块单例）.

findings.title: Structural drift: other
findings.body:
Standard: .trellis/spec/apps/dashboard/frontend/api-layer-contract.md §6（「**不排序、不剔除参数**」）/ design.md §1 被否掉的方案（`keys.ts` 里加通用 `norm()` 排序参数）
Note: The implementation checklist still instructs adding a `norm()` key-normalization helper, contradicting the key-registry contract ('结构恒为 `[domain, resource, ...params]`', no sorting/no pruning) and the design's own rejected-scheme table; following implement.md would reintroduce the discarded normalization layer.

findings.title: Structural drift: placement
findings.body:
Standard: CLAUDE.md#工程规范 (test placement rule, context line of this hunk)
Note: The repo rule keeps tests out of `src/` and puts them in a sibling `tests/` tree that mirrors `src/`. This PR's dashboard tests are co-located inside `src/` (e.g. `apps/dashboard/src/lib/api/http.test.ts`, `apps/dashboard/src/lib/api/keys.test.ts`, `apps/dashboard/src/lib/api/modules.test.ts`, `apps/dashboard/src/lib/api/api-map.test.ts`, `apps/dashboard/src/lib/query-client.test.ts`, `apps/dashboard/src/features/auth/auth-flow.test.ts`, `apps/dashboard/src/components/chrome/dashboard-header.test.ts`), crossing the source/test boundary the rule establishes. No diff content for those files was supplied, so the row is anchored on the standard line itself.
findings.recommendation: Align placement / naming / ownership with CLAUDE.md#工程规范 (test placement rule, context line of this hunk).

findings.title: Structural drift: ownership
findings.body:
Standard: peer:apps/dashboard/src/routes/$locale/dashboard.tsx:69
Note: Introduces a second, URL-string-based source for the current locale alongside the router-owned `$locale` param that the route module already resolves into `safeLocale` and passes to `createT(safeLocale)` / `useSignOut(safeLocale)`. Re-deriving the locale by splitting `window.location.pathname` (and silently defaulting to `en` for any non-locale prefix) moves locale resolution ownership out of the router parameter and into `lib`, creating two competing locale sources.

focus: intent:Pagination parameter names split three ways: `p`/`page_size`

repair_notes: triage-drift: first turn parse failed (finish=length, text_len=0, head=""); repaired

notes: The PR label is `review: low`, but the diff adds ~4.5k lines of new production code (transport layer, 14 domain modules, 401 single point, guard state machine) plus ~1.4k lines of tests — the label appears inconsistent with the change size.

Internal figures disagree across the PR body (85 pass / 195 assertions, gzip 147,442 B / −0.03%), verification.md (109 pass / 246 assertions, 147,939 B / +0.31%) and the workspace journal (110 pass / 250 assertions). At least two of the three are stale.

api-map.test.ts hard-codes `expect(rows.length).toBe(60)`, so the doc/endpoint count claim is enforced by the test suite rather than review alone; adding an endpoint later requires updating both the table and this constant.

The `failed` guard state is documented in .trellis/spec/apps/dashboard/frontend/api-layer-contract.md §7 (three error destinations must not be merged), so the code matches that spec even though the PR body does not state it.

query-client.ts deliberately exposes no module-level singleton; the app instance is created via useState(() => createQueryClient({ onAuthExpired: handleSessionExpired })) in __root.tsx, matching the body's 'injected at the app layer' description.
No reviewer comments or linked issues were supplied, so maintainer overlap cannot be assessed and no claim uses an issue source.

blockers.claim: Pagination parameter names split three ways: `p`/`page_size` for topup, redemptions, logs and aff; `page`/`page_size` for tickets; `page`/`size` for storages.
blockers.note: logs is implemented with `p`/`per_page`, not `p`/`page_size`: LogListParams declares `per_page`, api-map's logs.list row lists `p` and `per_page`, and modules.test.ts asserts per_page=20. Only callLogs/aff/topup/redemptions actually use `page_size`. The stated family grouping does not match the code.

blockers.claim: Verification results: typecheck 0 errors, tests 85 pass / 0 fail (195 assertions), build succeeds, dist gzip 147,442 B (baseline 147,486, −0.03%, gate +5%), bare-fetch audit 0 hits.
blockers.note: No CI output is in the diff, and the PR's own artifacts contradict the body's figures: verification.md reports 109 pass / 246 assertions and 147,939 B (+0.31%); the journal reports 110 pass / 250 assertions. The specific numbers in the body are therefore not corroborated anywhere in the diff.

blockers.claim: The invalidation matrix in modules.test.ts is table-driven and covers all 16 invalidation-carrying mutations (including 'invalidates only itself' negative cases), plus updateEmailPreferences write-back and logout clearing the whole cache.
blockers.note: The mechanism exists (CASES table with expectInvalidated/expectUntouched, write-back test, performSignOut clear assertion in auth-flow.test.ts), but the count is wrong: the code contains 20 invalidating mutations plus updateEmailPreferences, and the PR's own verification.md states 21 — not 16. The CASES table itself only holds 12 entries, the rest are individual tests.
